result:
Streamed parallel tool calls from Gemini and LiteLLM now get separate indices, so clients that merge calls by index no longer combine separate calls into one. The Gemini and LiteLLM provider test files pass (123 tests), including a new test for each provider. Ruff isn't installed in the venv, so I couldn't run the formatter or linter.

**Gemini** (`mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py`)
- Tool calls are now numbered 0, 1, 2… across the whole stream instead of always 0. Calls in one chunk get consecutive numbers, and later chunks carry on from there.
- To do this, the streaming function needs to remember how many calls it has already sent. `model_to_chat_streaming` takes a new optional `tool_call_counts` dict, keyed by candidate, that it updates as it goes. `_chat_stream` creates one dict per stream and passes it with every chunk.
- If you leave the dict out, it behaves as before (each chunk numbered on its own), so other callers still work.

**LiteLLM** (`mlflow/gateway/providers/litellm.py`)
- The chunk-to-dict conversion now keeps the index LiteLLM supplies on each tool call. It only falls back to the call's position in the chunk when that index is missing or `None`.

**Tests**
- `test_gemini_chat_stream_parallel_tool_calls_get_consecutive_indices`: one call in the first chunk and two in the second come out as indices `[0, 1, 2]`, each with the right arguments.
- `test_chat_stream_preserves_tool_call_index` (LiteLLM): interleaved chunks for calls 0 and 1 keep their own indices, and a chunk with no indices falls back to `[0, 1]`.

As asked, I didn't touch the Gemini finish reason or the Bedrock index offset.
